Content: Oscar Bobb, of Fulham, Brighton’s Malick Yalcouyé and Everton’s Vitalii Mykolenko.Composite: Getty, ShutterstockView image in fullscreenOscar Bobb, of Fulham, Brighton’s Malick Yalcouyé and Everton’s Vitalii Mykolenko.Composite: Getty, ShutterstockPremier LeaguePremier League: 10 things to look out for this weekendSpurs and Villa meet in desperation derby and Andoni Iraola faces test on south-coast returnPremier League top scorers: check the latest standingsGuardian sportThu 17 Sep 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 19.36 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1Bees sense chance to sting Blues’ backlineChelsea have not won this west London derby since Brentford’s first Premier League season. Each visit sinceOctober 2021’s 1-0 win, Ben Chilwell the scorer, has been a draw. This season has continued the divergence between the clubs’ respective approaches, Brentford’s solidity and continuity compared to Chelsea attempting their latest reboot. Kevin Schade, after two well-taken goals at Bournemouth, will fancy facing a defence not yet attuned to Xabi Alonso’s configurations. Only one team has won a Premier League title with a defensive trio: Chelsea’s last title team, in 2016-17 under Antonio Conte. Alonso’s attack has been rather more successful, presenting another challenge for Jannik Schuster. Replacing Nathan Collins, the 20-year-old central defender had a tough examination from Bournemouth’s Evanilsonon his first Premier League start, emerging with credit. For Chelsea, João Pedro has registered three goals and three assists, but doubts surrounding his fitness could lead to Danny Welbeck’s first league start.John BrewinBrentford v Chelsea, Friday 8pm (all times BST)Chart showing top players for goals scored above expected goals, 2026‑27 Premier League2Spurs and Villa meet in desperation derbyWhat happens when a very stoppable force meets an extremely movable object? We will be tuning into theTottenham HotspurStadium on Saturday to find out as 19th-placed Aston Villa arrive in north London. Both teams have scored just one goal between them in the league and are desperately hoping for a first Premier League win. The return of Pedro Porro is big for Roberto De Zerbi and that should bring theArchie Gray Experimentat right-back to a merciful end. No Premier League starting XI feels less settled than Spurs – most players look as if they are a mistake or two from being dropped – which has culminated in a side that seems governed by fear and continuously prefers to take the safe option. After coming off the bench against Everton and Liverpool in the past week, the injury-plagued James Maddison will be itching to start and take some sort of initiative for Tottenham.Michael ButlerTottenham vAston Villa, Saturday 3pmView image in fullscreenMateus Fernandes will hope Spurs can get their first league win of the season against Aston Villa.Photograph: Alex Morton/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock3Hürzeler’s scoring express meets championsWhen Fabian Hürzeler spoke about Brighton’s success being founded on them being “well structured” after their stirringcomeback against Manchester United at Old Traffordon Wednesday, he could have been referring to Malick Yalcouyé. The 20-year-old Ivorian moved to the south coast in 2024 after spending just a few months with IFK Gothenburg in Sweden but had to wait until this season to make his senior debut for Brighton after being sent on loan to Sturm Graz in Austria and then Swansea last season. With Jack Hinshelwood sidelined due to injury until after the international break, Yalcouyé has taken his chance in the No 10 role and already found the net twice in the Premier League as Brighton have made a brilliant start. Champions Arsenal are up next for the division’s top scorers – who have registered 13 goals from their opening four matches – and Mikel Arteta should be wary of the threat posed by Yalcouyé and co as they prepare for a fourth away game in succession.Ed AaronsBrighton vArsenal, Saturday 3pmChart showing the top players for non-penalty expected goals per shot, 2026‑27 Premier League4Mykolenko form a boost for MoyesVitalii Mykolenko’s early season improvement has gone largely unheralded so far – and probably always will be among his detractors – but at a time when David Moyes needs experienced players to step up and defy the constraints of a small squad, theEvertonleft-back has produced. Having signed a new three-year contract in the summer, and seemingly bulked up, the Ukraine international has kept his critics quiet with several impressive displays for a defence that has kept four clean sheets in six matches. There remains a problematic lack of cover at left-back after the decision to loan Adam Aznou to Málaga for the season but Mykolenko, the better defender, has eased the concerns that surrounded his position ahead of the new campaign. Ipswich’s new forward recruits, Emersonn and Zian Flemming, will test Everton’s solidity but Moyes’s side will have made an encouraging start should they sign off with a win before the extended international break.Andy HunterEverton v Ipswich, Saturday 3pmChart showing sides of pitch used for attacking by teams, 2026‑27 Premier League5Jaissle refuses to delete Newcastle blueprintAs befits a lover of direct football, Matthias Jaissle likes to get straight to the point. On Thursday he was asked if, in the light of Monday night’s4-1 thrashing at Leedsand a raft of injuries, he was tempted to perhaps switch to a back five or modify his beloved “vertical” approach when Hull visit Tyneside on Saturday. The reply proved unequivocal. “No,” said a manager unafraid to answer questions with a single word. Instead Jaissle expects his young team to retain faith in a wider vision as Newcastle – who signed eight players aged 24 and under this summer – adapt to life after Bruno Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. “It’s a brave journey the club is going on and I’m fully committed in that,” said Eddie Howe’s successor. “If there’s one setback, we shouldn’t delete our journey or our vision. We’re fully committed. We’re fully aligned. We anticipated that something like that against Leeds would happen. It’s on us to respond. But while still believing. We don’t change.”Louise TaylorNewcastle v Hull, Saturday 3pmView image in fullscreen‘We’re fully aligned,’ says Newcastle’s Matthias Jaissle.Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock6Delap hopes to impress as Wood regentMany scoffed at the £45m that was paid for Liam Delap in the summer butNottingham Forestfeels like the perfect place for the striker to regain his form. Forest previously thrived with Chris Wood as their arrowhead and Delap is something of a younger Wood regent – powerful, instinctive and willing to bring others into play. During Saturday’s away win at Villa, Morgan Gibbs-White and Delap looked as if they already have an understanding and both will be keen to capitalise against a Coventry side that has conceded eight goals in the past two games. After a nervy campaign last season, Forest feel back in the ascendancy and will have been delighted that plans to increase the City Ground’s capacity from 31,000 to 52,500, at an estimated cost of £790m, were approved by the local council on Wednesday.MBNottingham Forest v Coventry, Saturday 5.30pm7Iraola faces test on south-coast returnAfter watching Bournemouth make their European bow from afar in San Sebastián, a city Andoni Iraola knows inside out, the Basque head coach will return to his previous club on Sunday. Iraola – whose assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper played for Bournemouth, the former captaining the club into thePremier Leaguein 2015 – led Bournemouth into the Europa League after recording their best-ever finish. His body of work on the south coast earned him the Liverpool opportunity and a warm welcome is a guarantee. Despite the Cherries’ slow start under Iraola’s successor, Marco Rose, they will pose tricky opposition. Rose spent a couple of hours in Iraola’s company before officially starting in June and both will be braced for an all-action contest. Eddie Howe failed to beat Bournemouth in the eight league games he managed against them with Newcastle and Iraola and his staff will expect a tough test.Ben FisherBournemouth v Liverpool, Sunday 2pm8Calvert-Lewin: man on a missionDominic Calvert-Lewin will be a man on a mission againstCrystal Palaceat Elland Road on Saturday. Daniel Farke’s centre-forward hopes to become the first Leeds player to score in six consecutive home league games since Arthur Hydes back in 1932. Managers often, quite rightly, say that players matter more than formations but, in Calvert-Lewin’s case, Farke’s switch to 3-5-2 late last November proved a road to Damascus moment. Until then he had struggled as the team’s lone striker but, paired with Noah Okafor or Lukas Nmecha, the goals started to flow. Granted, Leeds sometimes play 3-4-3 or, occasionally, revert to a back four but Calvert-Lewin has emphasised the importance of attacking partnerships. After collecting eight points from their opening four games, Farke’s team have registered the best beginning to a top-tier campaign of any Leeds team since David O’Leary’s class of 2001-02. Will it continue at Palace’s expense? Is Hydes’s record under threat? Might 3-5-2 be the answer to ending more strikers’ goal droughts?Louise TaylorLeeds v Crystal Palace, Sunday 2pm9Le Bris plots party crash in ManchesterManchester City’s maximum 12 points from their first four Premier League games featured 1-0 wins (over Coventry and Manchester United), a 2-1 victory (Bournemouth), and a 4-1 success (Crystal Palace). Allowing only two goals while registering eight is an impressive record that is only marginally bettered by the champions, Arsenal (one conceded, eight scored in their 12-point tally), and it seems a rosy augury that Enzo Maresca’s team will be genuine title contenders this season. Régis Le Bris, though, plots to halt City’s perfect start, and can draw on guiding Sunderland to a share of the points last season against the FA Cup holders, though that was at the Stadium of Light. In the corresponding fixture at the Etihad Stadium, City cruised to a 3-0 win.Jamie JacksonManchester City v Sunderland, Sunday 2pmView image in fullscreenSunderland’s Enzo Le Fée reacts after scoring against AZ on their midweek European return.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters10Bobb needs to provide more end productOscar Bobb came off the bench against West Ham and fired Fulham into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with aclinical late winnerat the London Stadium on Tuesday night. It was a fine piece of individual play from the Norway winger but he needs to do it more often. The goal was Bobb’s first since joining Fulham last January and a player of his ability should be producing more of an end product. The 23-year-old is a clever dribbler and looked ready to establish himself at Manchester City before a serious injury curtailed his development. The talent is clear. Bobb had a good World Cup and should be full of confidence when Fulham, still seeking their first win in the league this season, host Manchester United.Jacob SteinbergFulham v Manchester United, Sunday 4.30pmChart showing carries of 5+ metres per 90 minutes ending with a shot or chance created, 2026‑27 Premier LeaguePosTeamPGDPts1Arsenal47122Man City46123Leeds4484Hull4385Brighton4876Chelsea4177Brentford4368Liverpool4269Everton42610Ipswich4-3611Nottm Forest40512Newcastle4-1513Man Utd40414Sunderland4-2415AFC Bournemouth4-1316Crystal Palace4-5317Tottenham Hotspur4-5218Fulham4-3119Aston Villa4-6120Coventry4-100Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueBrentfordChelseaTottenham HotspurAston VillaArsenalManchester CityfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Bill Belichick’s son resigns after investigation into UNC football turmoil | College football | The Guardian
description: Defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, son of head coach Bill Belichick, resigned after an investigation found that ‘certain actions’ disregarded school standards
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, son of head coach Bill Belichick, resigned after an investigation found that ‘certain actions’ disregarded school standards
Content: Steve Belichick, son of head coach Bill Belichick, has resigned from his role as North Carolina’s defensive coordinator.Photograph: Phelan M Ebenhack/APView image in fullscreenSteve Belichick, son of head coach Bill Belichick, has resigned from his role as North Carolina’s defensive coordinator.Photograph: Phelan M Ebenhack/APCollege footballBill Belichick’s son resigns after investigation into UNC football turmoilSteve Belichick steps down as defensive coordinatorInquiry finds ‘certain actions’ disregarded school valuesGM Michael Lombardi resigned earlier this monthAssociated Press andGuardian sportThu 17 Sep 2026 10.46 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 11.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNorth Carolina defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, the son of the team’s head coach Bill Belichick, has resigned as the school concludes aninvestigationinto its football program.The school released a statement Thursday morning saying Steve Belichick’s resignation would be effective in late October at the conclusion of a medical leave, which was announced early in preseason camp.Belichick denies he has lost control of UNC football program amid off-field turmoilRead moreThat comes after the school’s investigation “determined that certain actions demonstrated a disregard for Carolina’s values and standards of conduct”, according to the statement.The school said the actions were “isolated in scope” and “not a systemic failure”, and that “corrective actions” are now under way under the watch of the athletic department and the Office of University Counsel.Earlier this month, the schoolannouncedthe resignation of general manager Michael Lombardi amid the investigation. Lombardi was an immediate hire by Bill Belichick in his NFL-to-college transition.Shortly after Lombardi’s resignation on 3 September, Raleigh TV station WRAL reported the type of questions asked of some interviewees during the investigation. Some focused on Steve Belichick, withallegationsthat he was questioned by lawyers over issues related to drug use.Last week, reporters asked Bill Belichick whether he had “control” of the program.“If you’re around here every day, I think you’d see it,” Belichick said.The school later issued a statement backing the 74-year-old, who won six Super Bowl titles with the New England Patriots. The Tar Heels are 2-0 entering their ACC opener against Clemson on Saturday.Explore more on these topicsCollege footballUS sportsCollege sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Knicks halt sales after pricing ‘mistake’ puts season opener tickets above $1,000 | New York Knicks | The Guardian
description: The defending NBA champions paused sales and said they would refund fans after a ‘mistake’ caused tickets to be listed at extremely high prices
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The defending NBA champions paused sales and said they would refund fans after a ‘mistake’ caused tickets to be listed at extremely high prices
Content: The defending champion Knicks will open the season against the 76ers at Madison Square Garden.Photograph: Ross D Franklin/APView image in fullscreenThe defending champion Knicks will open the season against the 76ers at Madison Square Garden.Photograph: Ross D Franklin/APNew York KnicksKnicks halt sales after pricing ‘mistake’ puts season opener tickets above $1,000Get-in for game v LeBron James’s 76ers spiked to $1,408MSG Sports to restart sales and refund fans who paidAgenciesThu 17 Sep 2026 16.03 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 16.26 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheNew York Knickssaid on Thursday they are pausing ticket sales after a mistake caused them to be listed at prices that were too high.TheNBAchampions put individual game tickets for the 2026-27 season on sale this week. The get-in price for the 20 October season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers was more than $1,000.“We are pausing Knicks individual ticket sales due to a mistake in our pricing. We are rolling back to last year’s prices plus an average increase of 12%. We will restart sales with new prices shortly, and anyone who already purchased individual tickets will be refunded the difference,” Madison Square Garden Sports said in a statement.Will the Clippers’ $30m fine tame the NBA’s billionaire class? We’re about to find outRead moreThere is generally a ticket-price increase after seasons when the Knicks make the playoffs, and a jump was expected after the franchisewon its first NBA championship in 53 yearslast season. Owner James Dolan has not raised prices when the team does not make the postseason.“Our intention was never to overcharge our loyal fans, and we thank everyone for their support of the Knicks and their patience as we get this right,” MSG said.When the Knicks opened single-game ticket sales to the ⁠general public on Wednesday, the get-in price for their first home game hit $1,363, according to TicketData.com. The figure had spiked as high as $1,408 ​this week when single-game tickets ‌were first made ‌available to Knicks Fan First Chase cardholders on Monday.The process for purchasing season tickets began months ago and was not affected.The ‌season opener is shaping up to be one of the marquee games of the regular season. In addition to the Knicks coming off the title, the 76erssignedLeBron James and ‌acquired Jaylen Brown over the offseason to team with Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.High ticket prices have drawn scrutiny around sports this year. Secondary-market prices for the Knicks’ home games during the NBA finals in Juneapproached$9,000 for the worst seats at Madison Square Garden.The average get-in price for the Knicks’ 45 scheduled ⁠preseason and regular season home games is $262, according to TicketData.com. That ​is more ​than double that of ​any other team, with tickets to get into ​Los Angeles ‌Lakers home ​games averaging $130, ​followed by the Boston Celtics at $99.Explore more on these topicsNew York KnicksNBABasketballUS sportsTicket pricesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Robert Kraft, once the NFL’s good guy, is just another billionaire silencing Macklemore | NFL | The Guardian
description: The Patriots owner’s decision to ban the rapper from performing at the team’s stadium brings back memories of the blackballing of Colin Kaepernick
Author: Howard Bryant
Headline: The Patriots owner’s decision to ban the rapper from performing at the team’s stadium brings back memories of the blackballing of Colin Kaepernick
Content: Robert Kraft stands next to Donald Trump at the Kennedy Center.Photograph: Kevin Lamarque/ReutersView image in fullscreenRobert Kraft stands next to Donald Trump at the Kennedy Center.Photograph: Kevin Lamarque/ReutersNFLRobert Kraft, once the NFL’s good guy, is just another billionaire silencing MacklemoreHoward BryantThe Patriots owner’s decision to ban the rapper from performing at the team’s stadium brings back memories of the blackballing of Colin KaepernickThu 17 Sep 2026 09.14 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 11.02 EDTShareSix years ago, in the middle of a “racial reckoning” that never was, a White House that had begun out of control reached its chaotic apex. Federal officials were sweeping citizens off American streetsin unmarked vehicles, surrounding the Lincoln Memorialwith armed guardsand rolling military vehiclesthrough residential neighborhoodsin a fascist reaction to protests against the murder of George Floyd. It was at this point that NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, realizing it had all gone too far, appeared on a Zoom andadmitted his league was “wrong”for not listening to its players when they had protested against police brutality.The implication was clear: more than any other sports league, the NFL was harshest in its reaction tothe proteststhat began with Trayvon Martin in 2012 and continued with Ferguson, Baltimore and Colin Kaepernick. By blackballing Kaepernick, sitting by while broadcast partnersrefused to air the national anthemto undermine the protests, and, most embarrassingly, Goodell’s draconian announcement that teamswould be subject to finesif players showed dissent, the NFL had proven itself to act in the most un-American of ways.Colin Kaepernick knelt 10 years ago. America responded with a clear warning to Black people | Howard BryantRead moreThis week, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft showed he has learned nothing from those years.He banned Macklemorefrom supporting Ed Sheeran at the Patriots’ Gillette Stadium over the rapper’s vocal support for Palestine – something that has become a career-threatening political position as dangerous as kneeling during the national anthem. Kraft imposed his own version of authoritarianism:Macklemore claimsthat Kraft not only banned him from his stadium, but appeared to influence other NFL owners to stop the rapper from appearing at most of Sheeran’s other stadium dates. For his part, Kraft says his decision to stop Macklemore from performing at Gillette was due to both Macklemore’s “recent actions” and “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community”. In 2014, Macklemoreapologizedafter he wore a wig, beard and hooked nose at a Seattle concert, which critics said was an anti-semitic caricature.No NFL owner has worked harder to be seen as reasonable and socially conscious as Kraft. He has appeared on the surface as a shrewd businessman, power-neutral, making political donations to Republicans and Democrats alike. New Englanders recall him fondly as the man who rescued the Patriots from the misogyny and vile incompetence of the Victor Kiam years; from the threat of the team relocating to St Louis when he bought the Patriots from James Orthwein in 1994; and, of course, the man whosaved them from all the losing.Kraft was eventually given the benefit of the doubt as the hero in his stadium battle againstdisgracedformer Massachusetts legislature speaker Thomas Finneran that nearly led to Kraft moving the Patriots out of the Commonwealth. He did so by buildingthe only 100% privately financedstadium in the NFL – even though in 1998 Kraft himself had agreed to take a lucrative offer of public money from the Connecticut legislature and move the Patriots to Hartford. It was under Kraft’s ownership – led by his late wife Myra – that the Patriots took a stand for women, renouncing the rights to Christian Peter a week after drafting him, when multiple domestic violence accusations and convictions against the player surfaced.As the NFL collectively destroyed Kaepernick’s career (the former quarterback saysthe same tactics of collusion are now being used against Macklemore), it was Kraft who tried to appear sympathetic to those who suffered under systemic racial injustices. HesupportedPatriots Devin and Jason McCourty in their advocacy of criminal justice reform,helped the releasefrom prison of rapper Meek Mill, and following the deadly 2018 school shooting in Parkland, Florida,loaned the Patriots’ planeto students traveling to Washington to protest gun violence. Despite a president whocalled the pandemic a hoaxand encouraged citizensto inject bleachto immunize themselves against the coronavirus, Kraft sent his private plane to Chinato help transport shipmentsof N-95 masks to the United States. Bob Kraft has always believed he’s one of the good guys.In theMacklemoresituation, he is not. While he has been lauded by his supporters, all Kraft has done is follow a familiar script of a rich man applying power. He has undermined his everyman persona as a guy who sat on the cold metal seats at Schaefer Stadium alongside his fellow Patriots fan but was fortunate enough to eventually buy the team. Now he is just another billionaire using his power to stifle words – to do exactly what his fellow owners did to Kaepernick a decade ago. Nor should it be forgotten that no matter how many rappers treat Kraft like the cool old white dude, Bob Kraft, hater of hate speech, lover of peace, is a prominent part of a league that conspired to ban a player from playing football for telling the truth:cops are getting paid leave for killing people. That’s not right.Hardly hate speech.The end result is an old man threatened, unable to maintain the facade that he is any different, any better, than the moral rot around him. While truth often belongs to those who get to tell the tale, who control the airwaves, who get to do the blackballing and destroy the careers, it also belongs to the silenced. Both the overstepping Kraft and the tattered Sheeran – whose supporting actshave resigned from the tourin solidarity with Macklemore – know that now. One looks like a dictator, the other a wimp.Kraft is also displaying a perverse, pervasive strain of American exceptionalism normalized by Donald Trump where might makes right. His supporters have attempted to argue that Kraft hasn’t violated the first amendment over Macklemore because he owns Gillette Stadium, the land under it and paid for it with his money rather than with public funds that would be better spent on potholes, bridges and better schools. Along those narrow grounds, Kraft can certainly decide who gets to say what on his property – although even that argument is a specious one if he cares about community and not oligarchy. By then extending his influence from his private bubble of Foxborough to allegedly use that influence to blackball Macklemore from the rest of Sheeran’s tour by calling ahead to Philadelphia, Dallas, Tampa, Charlotte, Indianapolis and Atlanta, Kraft engaged in yet another collusion, for each of those venues are largely publicly financed. They do not belong privately to Kraft, or the rest of the football oligarchy, but to the taxpaying public. Public space is protected by the first amendment. Kraft has either forgotten what the pregame flags and flyovers are supposed to be about, or like so many other foundations in this country, has simply decided to stop caring.Where does Kraft stand today? The lover of peace and hater of hate speech is now backpedaling, remembering his position as one of the good guys, offering to throw money at the bad publicity –he suggested he would pledge $2m to unspecified charitiesin the Middle East without reinstating Macklemore – but he really stands with Trump, that most seasoned practitioner of hate speech,who once calledKaepernick and the NFL players who smash their bodies into a million pieces every Sunday “sons of bitches”.Kraft gave Trump $1m for his first inaugurationthen said in 2024that he hadn’t spoken to the presidentsince the January 6 attack on the Capitol.But there he satthis January in the Kennedy Center presidential box next to Trump for a screening of the Amazon Studios bomb Melania. As Trump petulantly destroys the arts, Kraft’s wife Dana Blumbergsits on the Kennedy Center board, part of the unanimous voteto close the centerunless Trump’s name is added to the building. Kraft has his name on another blackballing, but he’s headlining the marquee this time. For people who decry anti-democratic behavior, the Krafts seem comfortable in its company and quick studies at mastering it themselves. They’ve had a lot of practice.Howard Bryant is the author of 11 books, including Full Dissidence: Notes from an Uneven Playing Field, and Kings and Pawns: Jackie Robinson and Paul Robeson in America.He also writes on SubstackExplore more on these topicsNFLNew England PatriotsMacklemoreEd SheeranUS sportscommentShareReuse this content

title: LeBron James once raged against the machine. Increasingly, he helps prop it up | LeBron James | The Guardian
description: LeBron James was once one of the world’s most outspoken athletes. Now he’s plugging a predictions market and an authoritarian leader
Author: Karim Zidan
Headline: LeBron James was once one of the world’s most outspoken athletes. Now he’s plugging a predictions market and an authoritarian leader
Content: LeBron James and Will Smith were in Angola as part of the E1 World Championship.Photograph: Malcolm Griffiths/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLeBron James and Will Smith were in Angola as part of the E1 World Championship.Photograph: Malcolm Griffiths/Getty ImagesLeBron JamesLeBron James once raged against the machine. Increasingly, he helps prop it upLeBron James was once one of the world’s most outspoken athletes. Now he’s plugging a predictions market and an authoritarian leaderKarim ZidanThu 17 Sep 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 05.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere was a time when LeBron James’sviews on abuses of political powerwere considered dangerous enough that Donald Trump’s allies told him to shut up and dribble. But over time, James has become less outspoken. After he built a reputation as a voice on social issues and human rights, anti-government protesters in Hong Kongburned his jerseyover what they saw as his lack of support for their campaign. Alongside plenty of other US athletes, he has barely spoken on politics during Trump’s second term in power. There was the recent dismal sight of himpromoting a prediction market(althoughat least he kept his clothes on). Now he is happily associating with – and helping promote – an authoritarian leader.On Sunday, Angola’s president, João Lourenço, welcomed two of the most famous people in America – James andWill Smith– to his presidential palace.Officially, the two men were in Angola to attend a round of the E1 World Championship, an electric raceboat series featuring celebrity-backed teams. James and Smith are among those who have bought into the series.Lionel Messi earned $122m last year. He still felt the need to take Saudi money | Karim ZidanRead moreAccording to local media, Lourenço discussed promoting Angola abroad with James and Smith, emphasizing his particular interest in tourism, cinema and basketball. And there are valid reasons to visit and promote Angola.The country appears to be successfully tapping into roots tourism, with celebrities such as Smith and James leading the way. It has a significant connection to the African diaspora, with some researchersestimatingthat nearly 45% of enslaved Africans brought to the Americas left from ports in what is now Angola. The government is attempting to draw on this history to establish enduring ties between Angola and African Americans through heritage-based tourism. James, for example, visited the National Museum of Slavery during his trip to Angola, bringing global visibility to this connection.“Obviously there is a lot of history here,” James told local media. “A lot of history that not only is here in the country but also [crosses] over to America.”Meanwhile, Smith’s visit to Angola in March 2026 coincided with the International Day of Remembrance of the Victims of Slavery and the Transatlantic Slave Trade. During his trip, Smith was filmed discussing ways to support the country’s international tourism campaign.“We came, we saw, it was beautiful,” Smithsaid in an Instagram postas he left Angola. “And we shall return.”Some would say the actions of Smith and James are laudable, and in some ways they are. As members of the African diaspora, they are trying to help bring back money to a region whose wealth was stripped by slavery and colonialism. But they are also giving soft power to a head of state who oppresses his own people.Ahead of Smith’s visit, Lourençosigned into law legislationthat grants the government broad powers to monitor and suspend civil society organizations under vague claims of “security threats.” The law is the latest example of the increasinglyauthoritarian restrictionstaking place in Angola.Though Lourenço has enacted laws prohibiting discrimination against LGBT people, by 2024 he had effectively criminalized participation in peaceful protests when he signed a law enacting severe punishments of up to 25 years in jail for acts of vandalism. He also signed a law granting security forces the power to supervise media outlets, further restricting free expression.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWhile Lourenço tightens his grip on Angolan civil society, his government is actively investing in sports and entertainment with the intention of cashing in on the soft power benefits, a tactic that Smith and James are aiding with their visits to the country. Last year, Angola hosted the Fiba AfroBasket, which it won. In 2026, the governmentinaugurated three new stadiumsin compliance with Fifa and World Athletics standards. The stadiums boost Angola’s infrastructure and sporting footprint, allowing it to attract international tournaments. The E1 World Championship is merely the latest in its ambitious investments. Such campaigns are nothing new for Smith, who recently visited Egypt – another authoritarian country – and starred in acampaignfor a new real estate project in Ain El Sokhna along Egypt’s Red Sea coast.Angola is following in the footsteps of Rwanda and its longtime dictator Paul Kagame, who effectively used sports to legitimize his rule and portray himself as a pioneering figure in Africa.As the de facto ruler of Rwanda since 1994, Kagame has ruled his country with an iron fist, with his regime committing severe andsystematic human rights abuses. This includes forced disappearances, assassinations of political opponents, torture and state-imposed censorship. In an effort to soften his image, Kagame established partnerships with some of his favorite sports. From NBA appearances and sponsoring football clubs such as Aston Villa, Paris Saint-Germain and Atlético Madrid, to hosting international spectacles, the dictator is now firmly among a cadre of authoritarian leaders who exploit sports to enhance their reputations on the global stage.James is hardly alone as an athlete happy to give positive publicity to dubious regimes – Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have bothpromotedSaudi Arabia in a positive light, despite the kingdom’s myriad human rights abuses. Perhaps James could take a different approach – backing the people of Angola with his wealth and influence without giving legitimacy to the authoritarian who rules over them. After all, he’s already seen what that kind of figure can do in his own country.Explore more on these topicsLeBron JamesWill SmithNBABasketballUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Two years and one World Cup down, Mauricio Pochettino is still assessing | USA | The Guardian
description: The US manager’s first squad of the 2030 World Cup cycle leans heavily on youth, injecting intrigue into the four-game window.
Author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer
Headline: The US manager’s first squad of the 2030 World Cup cycle leans heavily on youth, injecting intrigue into the four-game window.
Content: Mauricio Pochettino has called in several young players for the US’s first post-World Cup series of games.Photograph: Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMauricio Pochettino has called in several young players for the US’s first post-World Cup series of games.Photograph: Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesUSATwo years and one World Cup down, Mauricio Pochettino is still assessingPablo Iglesias MaurerThe US manager’s first squad of the 2030 World Cup cycle leans heavily on youth, injecting intrigue into the four-game window.Sign up for our free newsletter hereThu 17 Sep 2026 13.15 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 14.37 EDTShareIn the moments after the USMNT’s 4-1 crash-out in the last 16 at this summer’s World Cup,Mauricio Pochettinotook the podium for what many assumed would be his last press conference as the US head coach. I had a question for him: “Would you consider your tenure here a success?” His answer was full of the usual platitudes, but one thing did stand out. He said, more or less, that he and his staff had finally gotten a good idea of the player pool.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionCavan Sullivan in, Christian Pulisic out: takeaways from the latest USMNT rosterRead moreIt struck me as bizarre at the time. By almost every account, Pochettino had been brought in to win the game that he’d just lost. Given just two and a half years to get it done, his job had never really been to evaluate the player pool; it had been to maximize results with the tools at hand, something he did with varying levels of success. And now, in the shadow of arguably themost disappointing result in US men’s history, we were finding out that it had been a fact-finding mission? And there were suggestions that he was leaving?That, of course, did not happen. Pochettino signed on to stay through 2030 –well, possibly– and on Thursday, we learned that he isn’t quite yet done studying the player pool. Far from it. Pochettino’s roster for upcoming friendlies against Canada, Mexico, Peru and Chile features 13 uncapped players, including four of the US’s five forwards; a further two players elsewhere across the roster have earned only a single appearance. The average age of the newcomers is 19 years and six months.There are notable exclusions as well: Christian Pulisic, who has only recently returned to the field for Milan after suffering a leg fracture at the World Cup, was left out of the US squad, as was Folarin Balogun, who has still yet to appear for Monaco this season. Weston McKennie remains injured. Given those reasons, none of the three omissions is particularly shocking, but they place the onus of leadership on others on the roster – such as Ricardo Pepi, who now finds himself shepherding a crew of teenagers up front, or even Sebastian Berhalter and Malik Tillman, who may be tasked with leading the youth revolution in midfield. FC Cincinnati center-back Miles Robinson, all of a sudden, has turned into the squad’s elder statesman, at 29 years old.Another set of Sullivan brothers are making football waves in BangladeshRead moreAll of this may conspire to make these upcoming friendlies – apologies, “non-official matches”, as Pochettino has taken to calling them – replete with far more intrigue than we’ve ever gotten out of a set of post-World Cup throwaways. This is unquestionably a good thing for US fans, especially those of us who have been clamoring for fresh blood.It also provides an opportunity for a bit of intrigue off the field. Pochettino’s pointed back-and-forth with another new call-up, 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan, in the media last week was the latest example of something he’d already made abundantly clear to others (Pulisic among them): mentality is everything. One senses that Pochettino is bringing this set of youngsters into camp not only to evaluate them as players but also as human beings, and to get a head start on instilling his preferred values in them. His lone quote from the press release that accompanied Thursday’s roster announcement says as much:“This is the beginning of a fresh start for everyone and we are excited in these first matches to bring a group of experienced players along with some young talents who have great potential. It will be important that they all understand our culture, our way of working, and of course the principles of how we want to play. Most importantly, they must show the commitment to representing the country in the way our fans deserve.”What better way, then, to show your commitment at the ripe old age of 16 than to face Mexico in friendly Phoenix, Arizona? Pochettino – and the rest of us – are about to learn a whole lot about the USMNT’s next generation.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US.Subscribe for free here.Explore more on these topicsUSAMauricio PochettinoUS sportsnewslettersShareReuse this content

title: Kluivert and Rayan rock Real Sociedad as Bournemouth win on European bow | Europa League | The Guardian
description: Two first-half goals inspired Bournemouth, playing in their first European match, to a 2-1 win against Real Sociedad in the Europa League
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: Two first-half goals inspired Bournemouth, playing in their first European match, to a 2-1 win against Real Sociedad in the Europa League
Content: Rayan is all smiles after doubling Bournemouth’s lead in the 20th minute.Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRayan is all smiles after doubling Bournemouth’s lead in the 20th minute.Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesEuropa LeagueKluivert and Rayan rock Real Sociedad as Bournemouth win on European bowSid Loweat Anoeta StadiumThu 17 Sep 2026 17.14 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 21.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe first goal that AFC Bournemouth ever scored in Europe could be heard out on the Bay of Biscay. A tradition from Real Sociedad’s old Atotxa ground, once lost but now recovered at Anoeta, dictates that a single flare is set off every time the visitors score while two are lit when the home team do; that way those out to sea know the score. And so it was that at 21.41 on a Thursday night in September 2026, Justin Kluivert found the net and a man named Juan Iturralde ran out into the street to let everyone know what had happened.Back in Dorset and high in Anoeta, where 2,000Bournemouthfans sang their way through this most special of occasions, they knew. They had waited their whole lives for this and it was a nice way to mark the history they made, their arrival announced to Europe with fireworks and a 2-1 victory in San Sebastián, the city where it all began for Andoni Iraola, the manager who brought them here.Pino kickstarts Crystal Palace’s Europa League rout of Lech Poznan to ease Sage’s worriesRead moreIturralde ran into the night three times – he went once more when Rayan made it 2-0 after 20 minutes and again when Sergio Gómez made it 2-1 on 57 – and might have gone more too. After a superb first half, Bournemouth had to hang on, sometimes desperately, in the second. For a while it had seemed a lead would slip away from their grasp for the fifth time in six games this season, but Djordje Petrovic came to their rescue with two astonishing saves from Orri Óskarsson in the final, dramatic minutes. They had done it, everyone at the final whistle. It had been some battle and they had given everything.That resistance hadn’t appeared necessary an hour or so earlier. Bournemouth had waited 127 years for a first European game and considerably less for their first goal. They had been playing 10 minutes and 43 seconds and when it came they celebrated it twice. A lovely shift of the body from Evanilson started it, the Brazilian receiving and releasing Adrien Truffert. The cross was perfectly placed, bent behind the defensive line for Kluivert to score.High in the north-east corner Bournemouth’s fans went up but down in the south-west corner the flag did too, it didn’t take the video assistant referee long to prove that was wrong, and allowing them to do it all again while Iturralde set off into the street. Truffert was on the run again soon after, Alex Scott’s glorious long, looped, curling ball dropping into just the right place for Rayan to head the second.View image in fullscreenJustin Kluivert fires Bournemouth into an early lead.Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesThere was an ease about the way Scott had completed the pass – an almost gentle turn of the ankle, the ball delivered as if by hand – and about the way he played. Amid the speed and intensity he glided. Around him, teammates flew everywhere, Marcus Tavernier especially, and Real Sociedad could not keep up. Three times they threatened from dead balls too: Evanilson headed the first off the post, António Silva headed the second wide and Óskarsson just about headed away a third. Songs from the corner sung to a backdrop of frustrated whistles from the rest of Anoeta.From the home fans there was relief when half-time arrived without the lead being extended. There was also a reaction, a dash from Ander Barrenetxea signalling their intent and an increase in volume. Petrovic made a superb save from Beñat Turrientes on 56 minutes and almost immediately Real Sociedad pulled one back. Gómez’s curling cross bent all the way through, past the outstretched legs and into the far corner.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionEuropa League roundup: Ferencvaros pile more misery on troubled CelticRead moreThis was a different game and a different place now, Real Sociedad’s version of Bad Moon Rising interrupted by an “huuy!” when Gonçalo Guedes’s effort was pushed past the post by Petrovic. Already this season Bournemouth had lost leads against Manchester City, Everton, Newcastle and Brentford, most of them late, and a familiar feeling only increased as Gómez’s fantastic ball sent Guedes through on the left, only for the Portuguese winger to try to cut inside rather than shoot. From the loose ball, Mikel Oyarzabal’s subtle, clipped shot floated onto the top of the bet.Gómez was not their only problem. Luka Sucic shot wide on 81 minutes and then Gómez slipped Óskarsson in for what should have been the equaliser. Petrovic though saved that and, somehow, stopped the Iceland striker from five yards in the final minute.Ultimately, the fireworks were finally over on Bournemouth’s famous night as a European journey that was once unimaginable was heard across the sea.Explore more on these topicsEuropa LeagueReal SociedadBournemouthmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Chicago Stars make a splash as Vlatko Andonovski joins as chief soccer officer | NWSL | The Guardian
description: The former USWNT head coach will start his role in Chicago immediately as he seeks to revive the club
Author: Alexander Abnos
Headline: The former USWNT head coach will start his role in Chicago immediately as he seeks to revive the club
Content: Vlatko Andonovski experienced great success in Kansas City with the Current and FC Kansas City.Photograph: Soobum Im/NWSL/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenVlatko Andonovski experienced great success in Kansas City with the Current and FC Kansas City.Photograph: Soobum Im/NWSL/Getty ImagesNWSLChicago Stars make a splash as Vlatko Andonovski joins as chief soccer officerFormer USWNT head coach will start role immediatelyAndonovski has won two NWSL championshipsAlexander AbnosThu 17 Sep 2026 16.29 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 16.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFormer Kansas City Current sporting director Vlatko Andonovski is already back in theNWSL, with the Chicago Stars announcing Thursday that he has been hired as the chief soccer officer of the last-place club.Andonovski’s tenure with the Current had ended just 10 days ago, as the team announced a mutual contract termination in a tersely worded press release that deemed his sporting director position to be “not the right fit”. As a head coach, Andonovski won two NWSL Coach of the Year awards and two NWSL championships. He has won consistent praise for his ability to built trust with players and staff – a significant trait in a league with ahistoryof allegations of misconduct by coaches at the professional level.The move is a much-needed boost for the Stars, who have won just five games this season. The team also finished last in 2025. Richard Feuz, hired as general manager in 2024, was fired earlier this year. Martin Sjögren, Feuz’s hire as head coach before the 2026 season, was let go in August.Saloons, school and specialty coffee: NWSL players enjoy new era of side hustlesRead moreThe hiring of Andonovski comes as the club seeks to stabilize itself off the field. The Stars have played this season at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois and will continue there in 2027 as they seek a new stadium downtown. An ownership consortium headlined by Chicago Cubs co-owner Laura Ricketts bought the team in 2023 at a $35.5m valuation.Andonovski was considered to be by far the most coveted free agent on the NWSL market, with ESPN reporting that several clubs around the league had inquired about bringing him on board either as a sporting director or as head coach.His exit from the Current, and the nature of its announcement, drew surprise from around the NWSL, especially given Andonovski’s long history in the Kansas City area. Born in North Macedonia in the former Yugoslavia, he moved to the midwest in 2000 as an indoor soccer player, playing for the Kansas City Comets from 2001 to 2005 and later coaching the team before moving to the women’s game and coaching the NWSL’s previous Kansas City team (FC Kansas City) to championships in 2014 and 2015. His success there and with Reign FC in Seattle led tohis hiringas head coach of the US women’s national team in 2019. He found less success at the international level, guiding the Americans to a bronze finish at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and thendepartingthe program after a disappointing last-16 exit at the 2023 World Cup.Hired as head coach and sporting director of the Current later that year, Andonovski led the team to one of the best regular seasons in NWSL history in 2025, winning 21 out of 26 games and finishing 21 points clear at the top of the table to win the NWSL Shield. However, the team fell short in the playoffs, exiting to eighth-seeded Gotham FC in extra time in the quarter-finals.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLast November, Andonovski moved off the sidelines and into a new role as sporting director, withChris Armastaking his place as head coach. The Current have comparatively struggled this season after the departure of several key players. Kansas City currently sit in seventh place, two points clear of the playoff line.Explore more on these topicsNWSLWomen's footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘I’m genuinely sorry’: Australian Hyrox athlete who soiled herself apologises to China and rivals | Australia sport | The Guardian
description: Joanna Wietrzyk posts that she regrets her decision to keep racing but has decided to forfeit her win in the Beijing race
Author: Martin Farrer
Headline: Joanna Wietrzyk posts that she regrets her decision to keep racing but has decided to forfeit her win in the Beijing race
Content: Joanna Wietrzyk of Australia competes in the Hyrox event in Beijing.Photograph: VCG/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJoanna Wietrzyk of Australia competes in the Hyrox event in Beijing.Photograph: VCG/Getty ImagesAustralia sport‘I’m genuinely sorry’: Australian Hyrox athlete who soiled herself apologises to China and rivalsJoanna Wietrzyk ‘regrets’ decision to keep racingShe forfeits points from her win in the Beijing raceMartin FarrerThu 17 Sep 2026 14.30 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 18.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Australian athlete who caused a storm by winning a Hyrox event in China despite soiling herself during the race has apologised to the “people of China” and rival athletes in a statement online.Posting on Instagram, Joanna Wietrzyk offered a “sincere apology” to the “people of China, my fellow competitors, the spectators and the Hyrox organizers for what happened during the race in Beijing”.Footage of Wietrzyk, a world record-holder,went viralafter it showed her competing in – and winning – Saturday’s event with demanding exercises and using communal equipment, despite having faecal matter running down her legs.But she admitted in her post on Thursday night that she should have “stepped off the track” and that there was “more to life than racing”.Hyrox changes rules and apologises for allowing Australian athlete who soiled herself to continueRead more“I felt completely fit and healthy at the start of the race, with no reason to expect any illness,” Wietrzyk wrote.“Looking back, I regret the decision to not have stepped off the track. I recognise that I should have made a different choice. I take responsibility for my decision to continue and am deeply sorry for the discomfort and disruption it caused.”She said she would forfeit the points from winning the event.“I know my actions had an impact beyond myself, and I am genuinely sorry to everyone who was affected. I am learning from this experience and will carry those lessons with me, including remembering that there is more to life than racing and knowing when it is right to step away. On reflection, I have decided to retroactively withdraw from the race and forfeit the points I earned.”Hyrox, an increasingly popular fitness competition launched in Germany in 2017, is now held in locations across the world. It made its debut in mainland China in late 2024.In each race, participants alternate between running a kilometre and doing fitness exercises at shared high-intensity stations – including a rowing machine, sled pushes, burpee jumps, medicine ball throws and lunges while carrying a sandbag.Hyrox earlier this week apologised and pledged immediate rule changes after Wietrzyk was allowed to finish and win the Beijing event.Hyrox co-founder Moritz Fürste apologised in astatementon Instagram to everyone affected “directly or indirectly”.“Hyrox made a mistake by not reacting immediately during the race. In the end it is my job to foresee these potential incidents – and I did not,” Fürste said.He added that Hyrox had made “rulebook changes immediately”.“As of this moment, there are new rules and procedures in place to prevent situations like this from happening again.”Before the weekend’s incident, event rules penalised athletes for minor infractions such as littering on the course, or spitting or clearing their nose on the floor. But they contained no immediate protocol for faecal matter.Ending her Thursday statement, Wietrzyk said: “Thank you to those standing by me, both as an athlete and as a person, during this time, and to everyone who has reached out with kindness and support. It means more to me than I can properly express right now. I will be taking some time to recover, reflect and look after myself and my family away from the noise.”Explore more on these topicsAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Pino kickstarts Crystal Palace’s Europa League rout of Lech Poznan to ease Sage’s worries | Europa League | The Guardian
description: First-half goals from Yéremy Pino, Chris Richards and Jørgen Strand Larsen and a late strike by Eddie Nketiah gave Crystal Palace a comfortable 4-0 win over Lech Poznan in their Europa League opener
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: First-half goals from Yéremy Pino, Chris Richards and Jørgen Strand Larsen and a late strike by Eddie Nketiah gave Crystal Palace a comfortable 4-0 win over Lech Poznan in their Europa League opener
Content: Yéremy Pino of Crystal Palace (centre) is congratulated by Adam Wharton and Jørgen Strand Larsen after opening the scoring.Photograph: David Cliff/EPAView image in fullscreenYéremy Pino of Crystal Palace (centre) is congratulated by Adam Wharton and Jørgen Strand Larsen after opening the scoring.Photograph: David Cliff/EPAEuropa LeaguePino kickstarts Crystal Palace’s Europa League rout of Lech Poznan to ease Sage’s worriesEd Aaronsat Selhurst ParkThu 17 Sep 2026 17.03 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 21.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt was worth the wait forCrystal Palace. After being denied their rightful place in the Europa League last season, Pierre Sage’s side made the perfect debut by brushing aside Lech Poznan with a victory that will take some of the heat off their new manager.The Frenchman has big shoes to fill in replacing Oliver Glasner after his predecessor won three trophies in the space of 12 months and there had been some talk of disquiet behind the scenes following his decision to drop the teenager Jaydee Canvot at the weekend. But while Palace face a testing trip to face in-form Leeds on Sunday, having conceded 11 goals from their opening four Premier League matches, they were given a big helping hand by their opponents here well before Radoslaw Murawski was sent off late on for a reckless foul on Canvot.Kluivert and Rayan rock Real Sociedad as Bournemouth win on European bowRead moreThe result was never in doubt after Poznan gifted Yéremy Pino a goal direct from their own throw-in, with Chris Richards and a Jørgen Strand Larsen penalty making the points safe by half-time. Eddie Nketiah rounded off the win with a late fourth and Sage was delighted to have shared in Palace’s historic moment before a meeting with his former club Lyon next month.“I saw a lot of videos about the fans, especially during the journey in the Conference League last year,” he said. “They were incredible and I want to share the same thing with them this year.”It’s a measure how quickly things have moved on in south London that Palace didn’t even have the chance to stage a parade to celebrate theirConference League triumph. But after a difficult start to the new campaign, the captain Dean Henderson had urged supporters to “park the negativity” when he signed a contract extension on Wednesday.View image in fullscreenJørgen Strand Larsen makes it 3-0 from the penalty spot.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAPoznan’s European campaign started on 21 July and the Polish champions were backed by a vociferous travelling support. They were almost able to celebrate a goal inside the opening two minutes but the captain Mikael Ishak fluffed his lines as Palace showed their defensive frailties again.As well as some noise around Sage followingSaturday’s defeat by promoted Ipswich, there have been concerns about the atmosphere at Selhurst Park after the disbanding of influential supporters’ group the Holmesdale Fanatics. But after Terry Yegbe’s disastrous throw-in helped Palace take the lead, they were treated to two more goals before the break.Europa League roundup: Ferencvaros pile more misery on troubled CelticRead moreRichards headed in a deep corner from Adam Wharton and Strand Larsen dispatched a spot-kick after Pino was brought down by Murawski. There could have been another in spectacular fashion after Yegbe hammered the ball into his own net just before half-time but thankfully for him the assistant flagged for offside against Strand Larsen.The Poznan fans decided that was the moment to perform the dance they have made famous. After their side’s poor first-half performance, it was no wonder that they preferred to turn their backs. At least they could amuse themselves by letting off a series of flares in the second half just as Pino came close to adding his second of the night.Ismaïla Sarr’s first appearance of the season was greeted with the odd boo after his hopes of a move to Liverpool were dashed in the transfer window. But the reception for the Senegal forward was largely positive as Nketiah also came off the bench to complete the job on a night that Palace will hope can kickstart life under Sage.Explore more on these topicsEuropa LeagueCrystal PalaceLech Poznanmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Floyd Samba’s debut double lifts Manchester City to Carabao Cup win over Norwich | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Teenager Floyd Samba scored twice on his debut as Manchester City beat Norwich 5-0 in the third round of the Carabao Cup
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Teenager Floyd Samba scored twice on his debut as Manchester City beat Norwich 5-0 in the third round of the Carabao Cup
Content: Floyd Samba opens the scoring for Manchester City against Norwich.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenFloyd Samba opens the scoring for Manchester City against Norwich.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersCarabao CupFloyd Samba’s debut double lifts Manchester City to Carabao Cup win over NorwichJamie Jacksonat the Etihad StadiumThu 17 Sep 2026 16.33 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 21.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFloyd Samba lit up this tie with a debut that will have the 17-year-old grinning for a while after a superb goal in each half ensuredManchester Cityadvanced to face Brighton in the last 16 in their defence of the Carabao Cup.Samba has an older brother by a year, Tyrone, who is also in the academy. Their father, Christopher, is a former Blackburn and QPR defender.Manchester City 5-0 Norwich City: Carabao Cup third round – liveRead moreWith a game featuring speed, awareness and a poacher’s eye, he hopes to make a case for regular first-team game time. Given the elite-level forward competition this will be tough, but tonight was a fine calling card.Samba said: “A debut like that is mind blowing. I couldn’t believe it – that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me.”For Enzo Maresca, a sixth successive win maintains a 100% record for his nascent project (barring the Community Shield) and points to how the manager is shrugging off doubts about succeeding Pep Guardiola.Of Samba, he said: “Satisfying for the two goals, the entire performance he was good. He didn’t play [before] as a 9, we tried in the last two or three days. He is very good at finishing so it was a very good game for him. He is not a 9 for sure but he was good.”View image in fullscreenRyan McAidoo (left) congratulates Floyd Samba after he scored Manchester City’s fourth goal against Norwich.Photograph: Nigel French /Apl/SportsphotoCity host Sunderland here on Sunday. Defeat Régis Le Bris’ side and Maresca will enjoy his three-week international break. You would not bet against them doing so – City are improving with each outing, as they did against Norwich.Many opponents are blown away at the Etihad, so for the 14th-placed Championship side to initially tap the ball about was impressive.Maresca’s formation was fluid and reaped a first dividend when Nico O’Reilly’s cross was fumbled by the visiting goalkeeper, Daniel Grimshaw. The ball dropped to Allan and he delivered it back across for Samba to cutely head home.City doubled their lead when Samba laid the ball off to Ayyoub Bouaddi, the midfielder hit the ball to Rayan Cherki and, as Grimshaw advanced, he beat the keeper to his right.Watching from the touchline, Philippe Clement hoped his side were not about to crumble as the first half neared its end. He was relieved when Samba, running in, was thwarted by a Grimshaw dive at his feet.Yet his men ended the period chasing City: an exhausting task that showed the control the hosts exerted. In a sparsely attended tie, this was precisely what Maresca wished – it meant that his main man, Cherki could be rested, as Ryan McAidoo replaced him for the second half.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideCarabao Cup revised fourth round drawShowFleetwood Town v Arsenal;Man City v Brighton;Everton v Newcastle;Sunderland v Brentford;Liverpool v Chelsea;Bradford v Peterborough;Fulham v C Palace;Bournemouth v Aston VillaWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Soon, Allan joined Samba in registering on his City bow. From the left, the Brazilian zigzagged in, beat Sam Field once, cut back to beat him again, then found the far corner with a lethal strike.Maresca will have been displeased after the restart to see a Norwich raid that swooped down the left and had the ball bouncing to Kellen Fisher in the area, but the right-back missed the target.Fisher’s profligacy was punished when Samba made himself a cert for the player-of-the-match award with a second. He collected the ball inside Norwich’s area and shaped a sweet finish into the far right corner, the helpless Grimshaw watching it sail by.Maresca was delighted with this and also the wider picture of how his side executed the gameplan. With each win he oversees, the Italian’s authority and stature grow, his appointment appearing ever shrewder.The game’s closing stages were lit up by McAidoo’s sharp finish: an apt end to an impressive City victory.Clement said: “After 20 minutes Manchester City started to get a bit annoyed because they could not create anything but then you get the first goal against and we need to defend better. In the second half we were more dangerous – I saw several good individual performances, but it is hard to take – six shots on target, five goals.”Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupManchester CityNorwich Citymatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Europa League roundup: Ferencvaros pile more misery on troubled Celtic | Europa League | The Guardian
description: Celtic suffered another European embarrassment as the Scottish champions were beaten 3-1 at home by Ferencvaros in the Europa League
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Celtic suffered another European embarrassment as the Scottish champions were beaten 3-1 at home by Ferencvaros in the Europa League
Content: Daniel Arzani of Ferencvaros races away after putting his side 3-1 ahead of Celtic.Photograph: Robert Perry/EPAView image in fullscreenDaniel Arzani of Ferencvaros races away after putting his side 3-1 ahead of Celtic.Photograph: Robert Perry/EPAEuropa LeagueEuropa League roundup: Ferencvaros pile more misery on troubled CelticHoops beaten again after chastening loss to RangersJuventus hammer NEC, Besiktas pile woe on MarseilleAgenciesThu 17 Sep 2026 18.36 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 19.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCeltic suffered another European embarrassment as the Scottish champions were beaten 3-1 at home by Ferencvaros in the Europa League. Just weeks on fromcrashing out of the Champions League qualifiersto Austrian side Lask, despite at one point holding a four-goal lead, Celtic’s defensive flaws were exposed once more.Martin O’Neill’s team also suffered a chastening3-0 defeat to rivals Rangerslast weekend and failed to deliver on their manager’s promise to respond. Bamidele Yusuf opened the scoring for the visitors before Mika Baur equalised late in the first half. However Kristoffer Zachariassen quickly put Ferencvaros back in front before Daniel Arzani’s sensational strike, on his return to Celtic Park, capped a fine night for Ferencvaros.Kluivert and Rayan rock Real Sociedad as Bournemouth win on European bowRead more“We’re naturally disappointed getting beaten,” said O’Neill. “We started off very brightly. We had a number of balls that were flashed across the goal and no one there to put the ball in the net for us.“Their first proper attempt, really, on goal yielded a goal for them. We came back into the game, got the equaliser just before half-time and then conceded a really poor goal. We’re hit on the break for the third goal. While we had a number of balls flashed across the box, even in the last 20 minutes, we didn’t get there to the front post a number of times that could’ve kept it alive and we’re beaten in the game.“It’s a huge frustration, obviously, but it’s also psychologically quite damning as well. It’s not the start we wanted. We have seven games in which to try and get some points on the board. Really need to concentrate now on Sunday [against Rangers].“Tonight was, I think, a European lesson for us in many aspects. We’ll get ourselves together. We need to re-energise ourselves as much as anything else.”Juventushammered Dutch sideNEC Nijmegen5-0 at home with help from two ⁠errors by the goalkeeper Nikolas Polster and Marseille lost 4-1 away at Besiktas as the first ⁠round of Europa ⁠League matches wrapped up.View image in fullscreenNick Woltemade of Juventus battles for the ball during the victory against NEC.Photograph: Alessandro Di Marco/EPAThe first howler from Polster allowed Nicolás González to nip in ahead of him ⁠and steal the ball to give Juve the lead in the ninth minute. A goal from Kerim Alajbegovic and a penalty ⁠from Nick Woltemade sent them in 3-0 up at the break.Zeki Celik made it 4-0 in the 75th ‌minute before Polster again ‌came out of his goal and failed to clear the ball; this ‌time it was Randal Kolo Muani who rolled it into the empty net to complete the rout.Marseille’s disastrous start to the season continued as they followed up three straight defeats in Ligue 1 with a comprehensive beating at the hands ofBesiktas, with the Turkish side scoring three ‌goals without reply in the second half.Earlier in the evening, Greek sideOFI Cretebeat Germany’sHoffenheim2-0 at home, whileRB Salzburgpicked up a 1-0 win away toLevski Sofiain Bulgaria.Explore more on these topicsEuropa LeagueCelticFerencvarosJuventusNEC NijmegenBesiktasMarseillenewsShareReuse this content

title: FA chair Hewitt demands Infantino release records of failed World Cup plan | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: Debbie Hewitt has written to Gianni Infantino, demanding that Fifa releases all documents relating to his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan and the decision to lift Folarin Balogun’s suspension during last summer’s tournament
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Debbie Hewitt has written to Gianni Infantino, demanding that Fifa releases all documents relating to his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan and the decision to lift Folarin Balogun’s suspension during last summer’s tournament
Content: Gianni Infantino is coming under pressure as he prepares to stand for re-election as Fifa president in March next year.Photograph: Zac Goodwin/PAView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino is coming under pressure as he prepares to stand for re-election as Fifa president in March next year.Photograph: Zac Goodwin/PAGianni InfantinoFA chair Hewitt demands Infantino release records of failed World Cup planLetter sent before Fifa council meeting on 15 OctoberInfantino under pressure before presidential electionMatt HughesThu 17 Sep 2026 14.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 18.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Football Association’s chair, Debbie Hewitt, has written toGianni Infantinodemanding that Fifa releases all documents relating to his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan and the decision to lift the USA striker Folarin Balogun’s suspension during last summer’s tournament.The Guardianrevealed last monththat Hewitt and other members of the Fifa council were lobbying for an independent review of the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) sell-off and the Balogun controversy. Their requests have been formalised in a letter sent to the Fifa president and his deputy, Mattias Grafström.Infantino installs loyalist to oversee Caribbean as he splits Fifa managementRead moreThe letter, first reported by the Times, has been sent in advance of theFifacouncil meeting in Zurich on 15 October. That is due to be the first time since the FFE plan emerged in July that Infantino will meet the other 36 members of the group that acts as Fifa’s board of directors.A number of members of the council, which comprises 28 representatives of the six confederations, eight vice-presidents and Infantino, attempted last month to call an extraordinary general meeting to hold Infantino to account over FFE and Balogun.The rebels were unable to get the 19 votes required to trigger such a meeting, however, and Hewitt’s call for the release of documents and an independent review is also likely to fail.Infantino has not had any contact with the Fifa council since writing to it to withdraw FFE at the start of August and has been lobbying for support before next year’s presidential election, making visits to the Caribbean, South America, Morocco and Qatar.Balogun’s ban was lifted after a phone call from Donald Trump to Infantino despite the player being shown a straight red card for serious foul play in the USA’s World Cup last-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. That allowed him to play against Belgium in the last 16, a match the USA lost 4-1.View image in fullscreenDebbie Hewitt is taking the lead in holding Gianni Infantino to task despite the risk that it could affect the UK’s chances of hosting the 2035 Women’s World Cup.Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images/PAFifa has said it followed due process, with the decision taken independently by its ethics committee, but has yet to publish a written report on the hearing. A request from the Royal Belgian FA for an explanation went unanswered.Hewitt’s letter is understood to make reference to other governance issues at Fifa, particularly its response to the crisis caused by the FFE controversy this summer.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe FA’s willingness to take the lead in holding Infantino to task comes with some risk because the UK is the currently sole bidder for the 2035 Women’s World Cup. A decision on the hosts of that tournament and the 2031 edition is due to be made at an extraordinary Fifa congress on 23 November.The deadline for candidates to stand in March’s presidential election is five days earlier. Infantino is the only candidate to publicly reveal his intention to stand, with Uefa and Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – working to find someone to stand against him.The FA sent a letter of endorsement for Infantino’s fourth term as president before the World Cup but, along with several other European countries, has since withdrawn its backing.Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoFifaThe FAFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Tuchel considers England recall for Cole Palmer in Nations League squad | England | The Guardian
description: The Chelsea forward is back in form after a World Cup snub, while Alex Scott and Morgan Gibbs-White are also in contention for England call-ups
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: The Chelsea forward is back in form after a World Cup snub, while Alex Scott and Morgan Gibbs-White are also in contention for England call-ups
Content: Cole Palmer has started the season with four goals and two assists for Chelsea.Photograph: Ian Walton/APView image in fullscreenCole Palmer has started the season with four goals and two assists for Chelsea.Photograph: Ian Walton/APEnglandTuchel considers England recall for Cole Palmer in Nations League squadChelsea forward back in form after World Cup snubAlex Scott and Morgan Gibbs-White also in contentionJacob SteinbergThu 17 Sep 2026 14.05 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 18.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThomas Tuchel is considering an England recall for Cole Palmer and could include Alex Scott in his squad for theNations League.Tuchel’s first selection since the World Cup will be confirmed on Friday morning and the head coach has been weighing up claims from a host of players who failed to earn a place in his plans last summer. Palmer was one of those to miss out after struggling for form and fitness but the Chelsea attacker has started the season withfour goals and two assists, raising optimism around his hopes of inclusion.Thomas Tuchel’s shot at redemption begins with England’s tricky Nations League testsRead moreEngland, whofinished third at the World Cupbut faced criticism for their performance in theirsemi-final defeat by Argentina, have a host of players competing for the No 10 spot. Tuchel took Jude Bellingham, Eberechi Eze and Morgan Rogers to the World Cup and snubbed Phil Foden, Morgan Gibbs-White and Palmer. Gibbs-White has started the season well for Nottingham Forest and is in contention. Fulham’s Josh King is another contender for a spot.King was one of four youngsters included as a training player for England’s camp in Florida before the World Cup. Scott, the Bournemouth midfielder, was also selected after failing to make the cut. The 23-year-old is in impressive form and was close to going to the World Cup. Scott is yet to make his international debut but is admired by Tuchel, who regretted not taking the Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha to the World Cup.England are likely to name an extended squad as they open their campaign in Nations League Group A3 with games against Spain and Croatia and a double header against Czechia. Tuchel could shake things up, especially as some players who went to the World Cup are injured. Dean Henderson, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, John Stones and Jordan Henderson have fitness issues.Players hoping to catch Tuchel’s eye include the Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and the Forest forward Liam Delap. The Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton is yet to convince Tuchel. Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite and Chelsea’s Levi Colwill are options in central defence and Newcastle’s Lewis Hall could provide competition at left-back.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe uncapped duo of Everton’s Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier are dark horses in attacking midfield. There is intrigue over whether the Real Madrid right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold will be picked after more than a year out of the international picture. Kobbie Mainoo’s situation is also a source of debate after Tuchel gave the Manchester United midfielder zero minutes at the World Cup.Explore more on these topicsEnglandThomas TuchelNations LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Alessandro Costacurta: ‘San Siro is an icon – it’s incredibly beautiful but it’s not functional’ | Milan | The Guardian
description: Milan’s grand old home turns 100 this weekend, and while it will soon be torn down one of the greatest players to grace it reflects on the noise and power of a unique stadium
Author: Nicky Bandini
Headline: Milan’s grand old home turns 100 this weekend, and while it will soon be torn down one of the greatest players to grace it reflects on the noise and power of a unique stadium
Content: Alessandro Costacurta: ‘The first time as a ballboy, it made me almost afraid. It felt like all those people were going to fall on top of me.’Photograph: Fabio Diena/AlamyView image in fullscreenAlessandro Costacurta: ‘The first time as a ballboy, it made me almost afraid. It felt like all those people were going to fall on top of me.’Photograph: Fabio Diena/AlamyMilanInterviewAlessandro Costacurta: ‘San Siro is an icon – it’s incredibly beautiful but it’s not functional’Nicky BandiniMilan’s grand old home turns 100 this weekend, and while it will soon be torn down one of the greatest players to grace it reflects on the noise and power of a unique stadiumThu 17 Sep 2026 10.12 EDTLast modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 15.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAlessandro Costacurta lasted 15 minutes of his first game at San Siro. He was, admittedly, not playing, but tagging along to watch his older brother’s favourite team.“I grew up in the province of Varese, north ofMilan,” he says. “So as a kid I was a Varese fan. It was my brother who supported Milan. The first time I went to San Siro, I was 12, my brother was 14. I think it was Milan-Bologna. But San Siro wasn’t covered back then, and suddenly this downpour started, so much rain.
